Foreign nationals can buy freehold property — full ownership of the unit and land — in designated areas such as Downtown, Dubai Marina, Dubai Hills Estate, Palm Jumeirah and Dubai Creek Harbour. You don\'t need UAE residency, and you can buy in your own name, jointly, or through a company.
Non-residents can complete the whole process remotely using a power of attorney, although most buyers visit at least once for viewings.
If you plan to apply for a golden visa, buy in your personal name — company-owned property usually doesn\'t qualify.
Set your budget — and the extra 7%

On top of the purchase price, plan for roughly 6–8% in one-off costs on a ready property: the 4% DLD transfer fee, trustee fees, agency commission and, if you borrow, mortgage registration and bank fees.
If you need a mortgage, get pre-approval before you start viewing. It confirms what you can borrow and makes your offer stronger.

Ready property lets you move in or rent it out immediately, and you see exactly what you\'re buying. Off-plan is bought from the developer before completion — usually at a lower entry price with a payment plan spread over construction.
Compare communities on what matters to you: commute, schools, rental yield, service charges and the developer\'s track record.
Ask for the service-charge history per sq ft — two similar buildings can differ by thousands of dirhams a year.
Make an offer and sign Form F
Once a price is agreed, buyer, seller and both agents sign Form F — the RERA-standard memorandum of understanding. It sets the price, the deposit, who pays which fees and the transfer date.
The buyer usually gives a 10% security-deposit cheque, held by the broker until transfer.
Make sure Form F includes a clear transfer date and what happens if your mortgage isn\'t approved.

The seller applies to the developer for a No Objection Certificate, which confirms there are no unpaid service charges on the unit. Fees typically range from AED 500 to AED 5,000 depending on the developer, and it usually takes 1–2 weeks.
Transfer at a DLD trustee office

Buyer and seller (or their representatives) meet at a registered trustee office. You hand over manager\'s cheques for the balance and fees, and the DLD issues the new title deed — now sent digitally, usually the same day.

What are the benefits of buying off-plan?

What additional costs should I consider?
Dubai Land Department fees, registration charges, agency commissions, and service fees. Our agents provide a full cost breakdown during the advisory process.
How long does a purchase take to complete?
A secondary-market transaction generally completes within a few weeks once documentation and payments are arranged. Off-plan purchases follow the developer\'s payment schedule until completion.
